clue.text: The murderer William imprisoned of course

definitions.note: read as 'a dish served as a course of the meal'

blocks.note: jug is slang for prison, so jugged means locked up
William Hare, partner of William Burke in the Edinburgh body-snatching murders of 1828

explanation.surface: A notorious killer named William is finally locked away, as anyone would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' looks like 'naturally', but it means 'served as a course'. The murderer comes first in the clue and the imprisonment first in the answer, as an adjective before its noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Hare stewed slowly in a covered pot is a traditional British main dish served at dinner.

clue.text: Bowler's mark, London

definitions.note: the answer is the first name that goes with this surname

blocks.note: first meaning: the small white ball that players aim at in lawn bowls
second meaning: the first name of the American writer of The Call of the Wild

explanation.walkthrough: Lawn bowls is played by rolling weighted balls towards a small target ball; the cricket bowler is a false trail. The second half wants the forename of the novelist London.
explanation.definitionFit: In bowls the target ball is called by this name, and the author of White Fang was Jack London.

clue.text: Cicero's expression Casca, didn't understand

blocks.note: surface reading: a Roman conspirator puzzled by an orator's phrasing
setter's reading: in Julius Caesar, Casca says Cicero spoke Greek and 'it was Greek to me', so the expression was a Greek idiom

explanation.surface: One Roman conspirator fails to follow what the great orator Cicero has just said.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Casca reports that Cicero spoke Greek, adding the famous line 'it was Greek to me'. An expression borrowed from Greek is the word wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or idiom taken from the Greek language, exactly what Cicero used and Casca could not follow.

clue.text: Trial flights of young ovine fancy

definitions.text: Trial flights of young ovine fancy

blocks.clueFragment: Trial flights of young ovine fancy
blocks.note: surface reading: a young sheep's first imaginative attempts to take wing
setter's reading: a young sheep is a lamb, so these are writings by Charles Lamb, and trial flights of fancy are essays, literally 'attempts'

explanation.surface: A fanciful picture of a little sheep's first attempts to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb published his essays under the pen name Elia; the French essai means a trial or attempt, which is where 'trial flights' comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb's celebrated collection of whimsical prose pieces, written under a pseudonym, are attempts at imaginative writing by a lamb.

clue.text: Wine flowing like water at the old festival?

blocks.note: hock is German white wine from the Rhine
the tide is water that flows in and out

explanation.surface: At some ancient celebration the wine poured as freely as water.
explanation.walkthrough: The holiday fell on the second Monday and Tuesday after Easter in medieval England.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval English holiday held after Easter, with games and the collection of rents, now largely gone.

clue.text: Looking so fast, so dissolute

blocks.note: first meaning: of a ship or car, smartly streamlined so as to suggest speed
second meaning: like a rake, a man of loose and pleasure-seeking habits

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' seems to mean loose living, which belongs to the second meaning; here it means speedy, the dashing look of a sleek vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes both a jaunty, speedy-looking appearance and the debauched ways of a rake or libertine.

clue.text: Its sight turned Moses into a law-breaker

definitions.text: Its sight turned Moses into a law-breaker

blocks.clueFragment: Its sight turned Moses into a law-breaker
blocks.note: surface reading: something that made the great lawgiver himself commit a crime
setter's reading: on seeing the Israelites worship a golden idol, Moses smashed the tablets of the Law

explanation.surface: Some sight so provoked Moses that the lawgiver became a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: In Exodus 32 Moses came down from Sinai, saw the golden idol and broke the stone tablets, literally breaking the Law.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden idol the Israelites made and worshipped while Moses was on the mountain was a young cow.

clue.text: A Venetian leader had a complaint when booted

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word before it is kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of Venetian
to ail is to be ill, to have a complaint

explanation.surface: A Venetian doge fell ill after being kicked out of office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booted' looks like kicked or dismissed, but the old verb 'boot' means to profit, as in 'what boots it?'.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic verb boot means to be of use or profit, which is what availed means.

clue.text: But better describing sixth form fare?

definitions.text: But better describing sixth form fare?

blocks.clueFragment: But better describing sixth form fare?
blocks.note: surface reading: something superior to how the top year of a school is doing
setter's reading: a ticket price, and a school form numbered one rather than six

explanation.surface: A comment on how the senior pupils at school are getting on, with something better on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The sixth form is the top two years of a British secondary school. 'Fare' is a ticket price, and the best travel ticket is form number one, not six.
explanation.definitionFit: The top grade of rail or air ticket, also meaning excellent, beats a sixth-rate one in every sense.

clue.text: A pin-up of a maid of honour

blocks.note: first meaning: a glamour photograph of an attractive woman
second meaning: a small tart with a curd filling, named after the bride's attendant

explanation.walkthrough: A maid of honour looks like a bridesmaid, but it is also a little curd tart from Richmond, a kind of baked dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for glamour photography of women, and also the sweet baked dessert of which the Richmond tart is one example.

clue.text: Catherine, the 100 per cent queen

blocks.note: shares at par are valued at exactly 100 per cent of their face value
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Catherine, a queen who was absolutely complete in every respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' looks part of the definition, but it supplies the last letter; Catherine Parr was Henry VIII's sixth wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine Parr, sixth and last wife of Henry VIII, is the Catherine wanted by her surname.

clue.text: Medium odds one form expert gives

blocks.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds when a race begins
the Roman numeral for one
a ritualist is a stickler for set forms of ceremony

explanation.surface: A racing tipster who knows the form quotes middling odds on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium odds' and 'form' read as racing talk; the definition is a medium of the seance kind, and the form expert is one devoted to forms of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium who claims to pass messages from the dead believes in spirit communication.

clue.text: Wind instruments so tunefully ethereal

definitions.note: a description of wind instruments, full of both breath and melodies

blocks.note: first meaning: wind instruments run on breath and play tunes, so they are full of both
second meaning: light, delicate and insubstantial

explanation.walkthrough: An air is a tune as well as breath, so wind instruments are doubly full of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Light as breath and delicate, without substance, as an ethereal thing or spirit is.

clue.text: First man to fly an aeroplane, or navigate a river?

definitions.text: First man to fly an aeroplane, or navigate a river?

blocks.clueFragment: First man to fly an aeroplane
blocks.note: surface reading: an aviation pioneer, someone like the Wright brothers
setter's reading: one who guides boats along a particular river in Hampshire

explanation.surface: A question about who first took a new aircraft up, or who steered a boat down a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a river in Hampshire, famous for trout fishing; a pilot on it would be its navigator.
explanation.definitionFit: The flier who takes each new aircraft up first to trial it, and punningly a river guide on the Test.

clue.text: Optic defect is found in bars, must remedy

indicators.note: to remedy something is to put it right, setting the letters in a new and correct arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drinker's eye trouble, picked up in pubs, needs treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term for a squint, where the eyes do not line up together, is an eye defect.

clue.text: Fool of a cat, dropping off !

blocks.note: a tom is a male cat
nodding, drowsy, as someone dozing off is

explanation.surface: What an idiot of a cat, falling asleep like that!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool of a cat' reads as one insult, but the definition is only the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a simpleton or blockhead; a noddy is also a dunce in its own right.

clue.text: This path up the aisle—or through the woods, say?

definitions.note: the answer is the adjective that describes such a path

indicators.note: say means we are to go by what is spoken, so a word with the same sound counts

blocks.note: a bridle path is a riding track through woods

explanation.surface: A playful question about which path a bride takes, to the altar or on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: The wedding word and the riding-track word sound the same; the wedding spelling is the one the grid wants.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridal path is the walk of a bride up the church aisle to her wedding.

clue.text: Limit not to be overstepped by servicemen

definitions.text: Limit not to be overstepped by servicemen

blocks.clueFragment: Limit not to be overstepped by servicemen
blocks.note: surface reading: a boundary soldiers and sailors must not cross
setter's reading: tennis players who serve, and who must not step over the back line while serving

explanation.surface: A boundary set for soldiers and sailors that they may not cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Servicemen' looks military, but it means servers at tennis; stepping over the line at the back of the court is a foot fault.
explanation.definitionFit: The back boundary line of a tennis court, behind which the server must stand.

clue.text: Jarrow man beheaded

definitions.note: doing double duty: a man with a bow

indicators.note: losing the head means the opening letter is cut off

blocks.note: one of the unemployed men on the 1936 Jarrow Crusade, a march from Tyneside to London

explanation.surface: A man from the shipbuilding town of Jarrow has been decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: The Jarrow March of 1936 is the famous protest of unemployed shipyard workers. The definition is thin: 'man' has to be read again as a bowman.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowman, someone who shoots with bow and arrow, is the loose sense of man meant here.

clue.text: With which 1 dn gets the wind up

definitions.text: With which 1 dn gets the wind up

blocks.clueFragment: With which 1 dn gets the wind up
blocks.note: surface reading: something that frightens the answer to 1 down
setter's reading: 1 down is also a word for a sailor, who hauls up the anchor by winding it in

explanation.surface: What gives a fellow named in another clue a fright.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 1 down also means a sailor (a jack tar); 'gets the wind up' means winding the anchor cable up, not taking fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolving drum on a ship's deck, turned by sailors pushing bars, used to haul in the anchor cable.

clue.text: Contentious data about financial statement

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps round the other

blocks.note: data are facts
an IOU is a written acknowledgement of a debt

explanation.surface: Someone disputes the figures given in a set of accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Given to forming factions and quarrelling, so argumentative and divisive in a group.

clue.text: This weight-watcher so upset!

blocks.note: surface reading: a dieter in great distress
setter's reading: the reason the dieter is upset, being far bigger than the usual clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A dieter is in a terrible state, probably after stepping on the scales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' wants to be an anagram signal, but the letters of 'so' cannot make anything; the clue just describes why the dieter is watching weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Larger than standard clothing sizes, which is why someone would join a slimming club.

clue.text: Colour of a banger

blocks.note: first meaning: a dark brownish red
second meaning: a loud firework or distress rocket that explodes with a bang

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a banger is a sausage, which tempts toward brown; here it is a firework that goes bang.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep brownish-red shade, and also the explosive signal rocket once fired to summon lifeboat crews.

clue.text: Involve the young devil Felix in a story

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: an imp is a little demon
a story can be a fib
Felix the Cat is the cartoon character

explanation.surface: Drag a naughty child named Felix into some tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Felix, which reads as a boy's name, is the famous cartoon cat; it sits inside the fib after the young devil.
explanation.definitionFit: To implicate someone is to show they are involved or connected, especially in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Singer who sang Sonny Boy to the end

blocks.note: Al Jolson had a huge hit with Sonny Boy in 1928
taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer who kept singing Sonny Boy right to the end of his career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To the end' looks like 'until the finish', but it says to put the word 'to' at the end, after the singer's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice.

clue.text: Bird's speed over the waves

blocks.note: first meaning: a small sandpiper of shorelines
second meaning: the sea unit of one nautical mile per hour

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird's' reads as a possessive, but the 's stands for 'is', linking the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A wading shorebird of the sandpiper family, and the unit of speed used by ships at sea.

clue.text: Old story of a young lady with a lisp

indicators.note: a lisp changes how a word is spoken, so we take the sound such a speaker makes

blocks.note: a young lady is a miss, which a lisper pronounces with th in place of s

explanation.surface: An ancient tale about a girl who lisped.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional legend, often about gods or heroes, handed down from ancient times.

clue.text: MP makes one, in topical reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, building these letters into a new shape

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Member of Parliament makes a point on some current issue of reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as a container signal, but it is part of the letters to be rearranged with the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A Member of Parliament is an elected legislator, one who works in politics.

clue.text: Celebrated dynasty

blocks.note: first meaning: praised in song or verse
second meaning: the Chinese ruling house of 960 to 1279, now usually spelt Song

explanation.walkthrough: 'Celebrated' reads as 'famous', but it is the past participle of 'celebrate in song'.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroes whose deeds are sung are honoured in verse, and the Sung were an imperial Chinese ruling house.

clue.text: Job of many round the City

definitions.text: Job of many round the City

blocks.clueFragment: Job of many round the City
blocks.note: surface reading: the work of lots of people in London's financial district
setter's reading: an army surrounding a town to besiege it, a task for many soldiers

explanation.surface: Lots of people in London's financial district work at the same thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial centre, where money is put to work; to invest a town is also to surround and besiege it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both placing money to earn a return, the City's business, and an old military word for besieging a town.
